newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Mayne eyes France's Generale de Sante.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Mayne eyes France's Generale de Sante.

text.p: Australian transport, security and health care group Mayne Nickless Ltd expressed interest on Friday in European hospital operator Generale de Sante, but declined to comment on a report it was short-listed as a buyer.

Mayne development director Clay Hayden told Reuters he had no doubt the group would be interested in the assets of Generale de Sante. But another Mayne spokesman said he could not confirm the newspaper report that it was a short-listed buyer.
"I have got no doubt we would have some interest, however we are still involved in Optus and we obviously would not be doing anything until we received our cash," Hayden said.

Mayne managing director Bob Dalziel told reporters on Thursday that unless the company sold its 25 percent stake in Australian telecommunications carrier Optus Communications Ltd by July, Mayne's growth strategy would be impaired.
He said Mayne needed to get its hands on that "bag of gold" to fuel an aggressive expansion of its health care business. Dalziel expressed interest in the European market.
The Sydney Morning Herald report estimated the cost of such a bid would be about A$2 billion. Mayne's Optus investment is estimated to be worth up to A$1 billion.
"We are looking to grow our health care business rapidly," Mayne spokesman Carl Kitchen said.
"If assets come onto the market we would obviously be silly not to look at them, but that's a world away from saying anything is firm or definite," he said.
Generale de Sante is owned by French conglomerate General de Eaux which has decided to quit health care.
